pressure_note: set pressure, taken by the authors as the vapor pressure of the solution at the vapor-disappearance temperature TM (footnote b); sample pressurized with CH4 as pressure-transmitting fluid (capillary nonmixing method), pressure transducer accurate to +/-0.097 MPa; absolute pressure not explicitly stated
title_as_printed: Measured Vapor Pressures of H2O Compared with the Data Calculated from IAPWS-95a

footnotes_as_printed.a: Standard uncertainties u are u(TB) = 0.5 K for 473 K < T < 693 K, u(TM) = 0.5 K for 473 K < T < 693 K, u(PS) = 0.097 MPa.
footnotes_as_printed.b: Set pressure, which is considered to be the vapor pressure of the solution at the observed vapor disappearance temperature (TM).
footnotes_as_printed.c: The temperature at which the vapor phase is generated at the set pressure.
footnotes_as_printed.d: Vapor disappearance temperature during cooling at the set pressure.
footnotes_as_printed.e: The corresponding temperature calculated from IAPWS-95 (42) for the set vapor pressure along the liquid-vapor coexistence curve.
footnotes_as_printed.g: Vapor pressure calculated from IAPWS-95 (42) at the measured TM.
footnotes_as_printed.j: Observed critical homogenization temperature in the HPOC.
footnotes_as_printed.k: The critical pressure and temperature of pure water from IAPWS-95. (42)
footnotes_as_printed.l: The set pressure at which no liquid-vapor phase separation was observed.

composition.other_species: pure water (DDI); sample sits in fused silica, which dissolves slowly, see quality remarks

skip_rows.reason: no measured TM: row 24 is the IAPWS-95 critical point (22.064 MPa, 647.09 K, footnote k), row 29 is the set pressure 23.0828 MPa with no liquid-vapor separation (footnote l)

row_flags.flag: TM is the observed critical homogenization temperature in the capillary (footnote j), not a vapor-disappearance temperature; the sample behaves as a H2O-SiO2 binary near the critical region
TM below the IAPWS-95 critical-pressure line by 0.4-0.7 K (Delta T negative), PS 21.2069 MPa

extra_unmapped: TB (K): temperature of vapor appearance on heating at the set pressure (superheated, footnote c), measured but not an equilibrium temperature
TC (K): temperature calculated from the reference model/IAPWS-95 for PS (from_literature)
Delta T (K): TM - TC (derived by authors)
PC (MPa): pressure calculated from the reference model at TM (from_literature)
conversion_needs: Footnote letters are in the note column; the pure-water reference data are reproduced for validation of the method
notes: 30 CSV rows = 30 printed data rows. Empty cells kept empty. Footnote letters on the column headers (b-i) are repeated in the note column of every row; letters printed on cells (j, k) are appended.
comment_reply_checked: 2026-10-02: the Comment (Cisternas, JCED 65:5062, doi 10.1021/acs.jced.0c00710) and the Reply (Chen and Chou, JCED 65:5064, doi 10.1021/acs.jced.0c00806) concern a modelling application (Cisternas-Lam correlation) and do not dispute the measurements; the Reply re-lists measured ternary pressures that match Table 5 (e.g. 2.5166 MPa at 497.65 K)
caution: Single laboratory, no independent corroboration; vapour pressures to 693 K in a fused-silica capillary cell, many points near or above the critical point of water; the authors attribute a shifted critical line to dissolved silica; molality basis (per kg water) and temperature scale not stated in the paper. A published Comment (doi 10.1021/acs.jced.0c00710) and Reply (10.1021/acs.jced.0c00806) concern a model comparison and do not dispute the measurements. Use with caution at T above about 620 K.
